problems.prompt: Implement 'groupBy(array, iteratee)' in JavaScript. It splits a collection into sets, grouped by the result of running each value through 'iteratee'. The 'iteratee' can be either a function (which receives each element) or a string property name. Return an object where keys are the grouping identifiers and values are arrays of matching items.

visibleTests.name: should group elements by a property name string
should group elements by a custom callback function

hiddenTests.name: should return empty object for empty array or non-array input without crashing
should group under 'undefined' string key if property does not exist on item

problems.inputHint: Implement in Cursor / VS Code or in Studio and click Run Test Suite
problems.checkpointHint: Check if iteratee is a function or a property key. Initialize an empty array for each unseen key.

steps.explain: Inspect the type of 'iteratee': if a function, invoke 'iteratee(item)'; if a string, resolve by property lookup 'item[iteratee]'.
Initialize 'result[key] = []' if the key does not exist yet, then push the current element into that array.

problems.prompt: Implement a robust 'debounce(fn, delay)' utility function in JavaScript. The debounced function must delay invoking 'fn' until after 'delay' milliseconds have elapsed since the last time it was called, clearing any prior timers and preserving 'this' and arguments. You can write and test your solution in Cursor / VS Code or in the editor below.

visibleTests.name: should not execute synchronously and only fire once after 60ms
should reset the timer on each subsequent call within delay window

hiddenTests.name: should preserve execution 'this' context and multiple arguments
should support 0ms delay as a macrotask deferral

problems.inputHint: Implement in Cursor / VS Code or in Studio and click Run Test Suite
problems.checkpointHint: Keep a single closure timer variable. Call clearTimeout(timer) on every invocation, then setTimeout.

steps.explain: Define a persistent 'timer' reference in the outer lexical scope. Each invocation of the returned wrapper must clear the pending timer via 'clearTimeout(timer)'.
Ensure 'this' and 'args' are passed faithfully to the target function when the timer fires using an arrow function callback or caching 'const ctx = this'.
